feedback.answered: A1: each leader creates a commitment object containing current voters and a startIndex equal to the first log index of its term. Local StoreLogs success and follower replication success provide match support; recalculate requires a majority prefix at or above startIndex before notifying the leader. A2: candidate campaigns use a fresh response channel per electSelf call, send one request per configured voter, persist the self vote and count granted responses; requestVote checks term, candidate eligibility, prior persisted vote and log freshness. A leader creates fresh replication/commitment state and a no-op; on leaving leadership it closes replication stop channels, fails inflight/verification futures and clears leader state. These mechanisms connect authority tenure to eligible support rather than carrying the previous commitment object into a new term. Configuration changes are admitted only after the latest configuration and an entry in the current term are committed. Follower appendEntries rejects old terms, validates the preceding term, truncates conflicting supplied entries, stores replacements, and then advances commitment to min(LeaderCommitIndex, local last index). The producer independently captures LeaderCommitIndex and limits supplied entries to MaxAppendEntries. processLogs queues local command entries through fsmMutateCh; FSM.Apply has an interface promise that entries are committed by a majority. This identifies a question about a bounded matching request followed by a divergent local suffix, not yet an executed violation.
